markdown_report:
The best next step is a frozen-SASRec transition correction with explicit controls for popularity and pair information. At 10% progress, this offers a small, reversible experiment; no validation improvement has yet been demonstrated.

**Insights from the starting point.** (1) Electronics has a 14.95% sampled negative-win rate versus 3.03% for Movies_and_TV. This motivates category-specific analysis, but training-pair margins do not establish validation HR@10. (2) User diagnosis favors recent, specific connections. Last-item transitions provide an observable proxy for these connections, although they cannot establish compatibility or immediate demand. (3) Sparse transition counts need shrinkage. Keeping a zero correction weight preserves the trained baseline and makes regression detectable.

**Insights from related work.** (1) *Measuring Recency Bias* warns against excessive recency emphasis [1]. Preserve SASRec’s full-history representation and test a bounded correction. (2) Sampled ranking can disagree with full-catalog ranking [2]. Select using the pinned evaluator and label full-catalog diagnostics separately. (3) Repeated validation feedback can overfit selection [3]. Predeclare a small comparison set and record every query.

These insights organize into three directions: local sequence evidence, uncertainty-aware backoff, and controlled validation.

| Direction | Existing mechanism | Proposed extension | Remaining gap |
|---|---|---|---|
| Sequence evidence | SASRec history features | Last-item transition residual | Latest item may be irrelevant |
| Sparse evidence | Empirical transition counts | Popularity-centered shrinkage | Rare pairs remain uncertain |
| Evaluation | Fixed sampled HR@10 | Matched controls and paired differences | Adaptive selection uncertainty |

Three candidate algorithms follow. Scores are originality/potential/difficulty; higher difficulty means harder implementation. Each assessment gives a positive and negative reason.

| Idea | Scores | Critical assessment |
|---|---|---|
| Shrunk transition residual [1,2] | 4/7/3 | Originality: interpretable combination; familiar components. Potential: cheap controlled improvement; sparse support. Difficulty: sparse lookup is simple; inference parity needs care. |
| Support-weighted recent-window residual [1] | 5/7/4 | Originality: combines multiple anchors; resembles recency mixtures. Potential: tolerates noisy latest items; may dilute useful transitions. Difficulty: reuses counts; adds weighting choices. |
| Training-count popularity correction [2] | 2/5/2 | Originality: clean control; established technique. Potential: identifies frequency effects; ignores pair identity. Difficulty: one lookup; coefficient selection remains necessary. |

**Selected algorithm.** From training histories only, count adjacent transitions \(c_{ab}\), source totals \(n_a\), and smoothed destination frequencies \(q_b\). Define \(r(a,b)=(c_{ab}-n_aq_b)/(n_a+\tau)\). This is a shrunk conditional-probability deviation; unsupported sources yield zero. Score candidates with \(s'(h,b)=s_{SASRec}(h,b)+\lambda r(last(h),b)\).

```text
freeze trained SASRec; build sparse training counts
predeclare a small tau/lambda grid, including lambda=0
compare intact residual, popularity-only control,
    and destination-shuffled edges preserving marginals
select by fixed four-category macro validation HR@10
serialize counts, configuration, and matching predictor
```

Use identical candidate sets for comparisons; report per-category changes and paired bootstrap intervals as descriptive [2,3]. Retain all routing, seeds, trial-local artifacts, and diagnostic interfaces. Measure both neural and deployed margins through the shared scorer. Twenty-user feedback remains hypothesis-generating; unavailable ratings, compatibility facts, and simulator traits must remain unknown.

idea.description: Add a popularity-centered, support-shrunk adjacent-transition residual to each category’s frozen SASRec scores. For training transition counts c_ab, source totals n_a, and smoothed destination probabilities q_b, use r(a,b)=(c_ab−n_a*q_b)/(n_a+tau), then score s'(h,b)=s_SASRec(h,b)+lambda*r(last(h),b). An empty history receives zero correction. Include lambda=0 and controls isolating popularity effects from transition-pair information.
idea.motivation: Electronics shows weaker measured training-pair separation, while qualitative feedback suggests broad historical similarity sometimes misses current purpose. Transition counts offer a cheap observable proxy for specific sequential connections. These observations motivate an experiment; they do not establish that transitions will improve validation HR@10 or reveal user intent.
idea.implementation_notes: Compute statistics separately for all four datasets using training histories only. Define q from destination counts with positive additive smoothing over real items; exclude padding. Store sparse counts, source totals, q, tau, and lambda beneath the trial directory. Keep DATA_DIR=os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR'], preprocessing seed 0, training seed 42, and the environment default SASREC_EPOCHS=200. Predeclare a small calibration grid with lambda=0 and select solely by pinned four-category macro validation HR@10. For the popularity-only control, retain −n_a*q_b/(n_a+tau) and remove c_ab/(n_a+tau). Shuffle edge destinations while preserving source and destination counts to test pair identity. Update the predictor writer and deployed diagnostic scorer together. For B×L diagnostic features, apply the correction using the source item at each corresponding sequence position, with padding masked. Retain DiagnosisProbe(view, device), run_full_diagnosis(train_loader), and diagnosis_interpreter_prompt(raw_diagnosis); return measured metrics and definitions. Preserve the actual trained model and compatibility hooks. No additional neural training is required for correction calibration. No performance gains are asserted.
idea.pseudocode:
for dataset in four_datasets:
    model = trained_sasrec[dataset]
    counts = adjacent_transition_counts(training_histories[dataset])
    n = source_totals(counts)
    q = smoothed_destination_distribution(counts, exclude_padding=True)
    residual(a, b, tau) = (counts[a,b] - n[a]*q[b]) / (n[a]+tau)
    score(history, candidates) = model.score(history, candidates) + lambda*residual(last_nonpadding(history), candidates, tau)
predeclare_small_grid_including_zero_correction()
compare_baseline_intact_popularity_only_and_marginal_preserving_shuffles()
select_using_pinned_macro_validation_HR10()
serialize_trial_local_statistics_and_write_matching_predictor()
run_architecture_compatible_diagnostics_with_measured_definitions()

originality.positive: Combines a support-dependent transition residual with explicit controls that distinguish pair information from frequency effects.
originality.negative: Markov transitions, popularity centering, shrinkage, and additive score fusion are established techniques.

future_potential.positive: Provides a low-cost experiment that can motivate support-aware or multiple-anchor extensions if intact pair information improves validation.
future_potential.negative: Sparse transitions and ambiguous latest interactions may limit gains; the supplied evidence includes no validation results.

code_difficulty.positive: Requires sparse counting and score lookups without changing or retraining the neural architecture.
code_difficulty.negative: Correct dataset routing, diagnostic position alignment, shuffled controls, and generated-predictor parity require careful integration.

related_work.title: Measuring Recency Bias (2024)
contributions: The supplied research summary reports that excessive emphasis on recent interactions can hurt recommendation accuracy.
Motivates retaining the full-history SASRec score and evaluating the strength of any recent-item correction.
limitations: Does not establish that the proposed transition residual improves this benchmark.
Recency sensitivity does not directly identify a user's current purpose.

related_work.title: On Sampled Metrics for Item Recommendation — Krichene and Rendle
contributions: Establishes inconsistency between sampled recommendation metrics and their full-catalog counterparts.
Supports keeping the pinned sampled evaluation objective distinct from full-catalog diagnostic recommendations.
limitations: Does not prescribe an optimal correction for the fixed RecHarness evaluator.
Metric analysis alone does not establish real-user preference alignment.

related_work.title: The Reusable Holdout: Preserving Validity in Adaptive Data Analysis
contributions: Explains how adaptive reuse of held-out feedback can undermine generalization.
Motivates limiting calibration queries and recording all attempted configurations.
limitations: A small predefined search does not eliminate selection bias.
The proposed experiment does not implement the paper's reusable-holdout mechanism.

related_work.title: The Hitchhiker’s Guide to Testing Statistical Significance in Natural Language Processing
contributions: Provides methodological guidance for paired statistical comparisons, including bootstrap methods.
Supports resampling matched user outcomes within categories when summarizing validation differences.
limitations: Bootstrap intervals condition on the trained models and fixed sampled candidates.
They do not account for adaptive winner selection or training-seed variability.
